sections.title: időpont: a time slot
sections.content: időpont literally means "time-point" and is the word for a booked appointment or slot — with a doctor, a class, anything with a specific time attached. Van egy időpontom ("I have an appointment") plus -kor tells someone exactly when. foglalt means "busy/taken"; szabad means "free" — the same szabad from szabadnap back in Unit 1.

items.spanish: Van egy időpontom a fogorvosnál pénteken.
items.english: I have an appointment at the dentist's on Friday.
Are you free or busy on Thursday?

sections.content: fogorvos is built from fog ("tooth") plus orvos ("doctor") — once you know that pattern, you can guess plenty of other -orvos compounds you'll meet later.
a fogorvosnál uses -nál/-nél, "at [someone]'s place" — a new suffix you'll see more of soon. For now, just recognize fogorvosnál as a fixed chunk meaning "at the dentist's".
